originality.rationale: The concrete claim is not a generic assertion of unimodality. It identifies the unique viability-versus-per-stage-speed phase frontier for every integer stage count, two and only two finite-deadline preference reversals despite worse mean transit and eventual viability, a nondegenerate square-root onset, sharp high-viability-ratio scaling and the large-stage limit. General monotone quotient rules supply an acknowledged technique but do not by themselves give these model-specific thresholds, sharp constants or counterintuitive reversal. The relevant ecological works describe matrix dormancy and long-term stepping-stone importance without this exact finite-deadline theorem. Searches and inspected literature support best-knowledge novelty, not proof of historical priority.
residual_risks: The standard monotone quotient principle is an acknowledged prior ingredient; closely related distribution-comparison results might contain an implicit equivalent special case despite search differences.

value.rationale: The mathematically natural operational question is which of direct crossing or a sequence of possible intermediate stepping-stone connections reaches a temporary target before a deadline. Incomplete-habitat connectivity is an ecological concern documented by Szojka and Germain (2024) and Saura et al. (2013). The exact frontier separates 0, 1 tangential, and 2 transversal deadline reversals for any stage count, even where both mean transit and ultimate success favor the direct route. The k-dependent c_k and sharp speed scaling quantify what additional stage count costs. This is a transferable falsification benchmark for ranking routes by eventual success or mean time; no claim of field-calibrated management value.
